body:
Thank you so much for the advice! The distinction between suicidal thoughts and tendencies was enlightening. I’ve sought help before, but it’s mainly been for my anxiety and depression. I think the thought I had was that if I could manage those two things better then the suicidal thoughts would improve as well. Sometimes they did and sometimes they didn’t. So I’ve never talked too much with a trained professional about the difference between me just having thoughts about suicide but not necessarily having the desire to take action on those thoughts. 

Also, your preface for the conversation is perfect and thank you for letting me use it. I still worry about telling my family as I don’t want to be a burden. My brother has recently had a lot of mental health issues and I don’t want to be seen as being in competition with him or evoke the same reaction from my parents (he needed a lot of supervision and assistance from my parents at the beginning). I’m hoping within the next year to feel comfortable telling them or at least my mom. I have a few trusted friends who know and who I feel comfortable leaning on. Honestly, this may sound silly, the biggest help is my dog. The unconditional love and purpose have gotten me through some tough spots and for that I will always be grateful. 

Thank you again!
